subtitle: When the Western Marches Held the Line

panels.shot: epic split composition, half showing a dusty frontier battlefield, half a copper plate glowing in a scribe’s hands
panels.action: Nagabhata I stands resolute on a rocky Rajasthan ridge with a distant camp behind him, while Avanijanashraya Pulakesiraja holds a gleaming copper plate in coastal Gujarat, waves and palm trees at his back.

dialogue.text: In the shadow of Sindh’s new rulers, Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya rose, and the Navsari tablet quietly marked the moment India’s western frontier pushed back.

i18n.hi: सिंध के नए सुलतानों की छाया में नागभट्ट और अवनिजनश्रय उठे, और चुपचाप नवसारी ताम्रपत्र ने वो घड़ी दर्ज की जब भारत की पश्चिमी सरहद ने पलटवार किया।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Indus delta and Sindh, fading into the Thar and Gujarat coast
panels.action: An expansive landscape shows the Indus winding through Sindh towards the sea, with caravan tracks heading east across desert and ships off the Gujarat coast.

dialogue.text: By the early 700s, Sindh had fallen to new Arab governors. From the Indus delta, their armies probed east, testing Rajasthan, Malwa and Gujarat.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी के शुरू तक सिंध नए अरब सूबेदारों के हाथ गिर चुका था। सिंधु के मुहाने से उनकी फौजें पूरब बढ़ीं, राजस्थान, मालवा और गुजरात को परखती हुईं।

panels.shot: mid-shot of an Arab commander conferring with local allies inside a palm-shaded camp
panels.action: Within a palm-fringed camp near the Indus, an Arab commander in simple mail gestures east over a rough map while local intermediaries listen, horses resting nearby.

dialogue.text: Arabic chroniclers remembered bold expeditions from Sindh, governors driving small but sharp forces into the old Indian realms, seeking tribute and footholds.

i18n.hi: अरबी इतिहासकारों ने सिंध से निकली दिलेर मुहिमों को याद रखा, सूबेदार जो छोटी पर धारदार टुकड़ियाँ पुरानी भारतीय रियासतों में घुसा कर नज़राना और पाँव जमाने की जगहें तलाशते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on the Navsari copper plate being engraved by a court scribe
panels.action: In a lamplit chamber, Avanijanashraya Pulakesiraja stands over a seated scribe who carefully incises Sanskrit lines into a shining copper plate.

dialogue.text: But the clearest Indian voice from that frontier storm came not from a poem, but from metal. Near Navsari, a copper-plate grant recorded a victory in sober, legal Sanskrit.

i18n.hi: पर उस तूफानी सरहद की सबसे साफ़ भारतीय गवाही कविता नहीं, धातु से आई। नवसारी के पास एक ताम्रपत्र में सधी, कानूनी संस्कृत में जीत लिखी गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Avanijanashraya in armor on the Konkan coast, looking inland
panels.action: Avanijanashraya Pulakesiraja, in mail and cloth, stands on a rocky Gujarat shoreline, waves crashing behind him as he gazes inland toward faint smoke on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Avanijanashraya Pulakesiraja, a Chalukya viceroy in coastal Gujarat, called himself the shield of his overlord. His plate speaks of a Tajika army pushing towards Navsari around 738 or 739.

i18n.hi: समुद्री गुजरात का चालुक्य शासक अवनिजनश्रय पुलकेशिराज खुद को अपने महाराज का कवच कहता है। उसके ताम्रपत्र में ताजिक फौज के ७३८–७३९ के आसपास नवसारी की ओर बढ़ने की खबर है।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Avanijanashraya briefing local chiefs atop a fortress wall
panels.action: On the stone ramparts of a coastal fort, Avanijanashraya addresses gathered local chiefs and soldiers, pointing inland as banners stir in the sea breeze.

dialogue.text: The grant boasts that he drove back a Tajika host near Navsari, saving his king’s realm and the land’s sacred places. It is royal praise, but even praise carries clues.

i18n.hi: दानपत्र इतराता है कि उसने नवसारी के पास ताजिक सेना को पछाड़ा, अपने राजा की धरती और पवित्र धाम बचाए। यह राजकीय श्लाघा है, पर श्लाघा में भी सुराग छिपे हैं।

panels.shot: map-like wide shot showing arrows from Sindh into Rajasthan, Malwa and Gujarat
panels.action: A stylised landscape shows faint arrows pushing east from Sindh towards Rajasthan’s deserts, Malwa’s plateau and Gujarat’s coast, with small fort symbols resisting.

dialogue.text: Across the same decades, Gwalior’s later inscription of Bhoja I recalled Nagabhata I holding against a mlechchha army in the west. Arabic writers too spoke of setbacks in those lands.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं दशकों में ग्वालियर के भोज प्रथम के शिलालेख ने याद किया कि नागभट्ट प्रथम ने पश्चिम में एक म्लेच्छ सेना को रोके रखा। अरबी लेख भी इन्हीं इलाकों की नाकाम मोहिमों का ज़िक्र करते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Nagabhata on a rugged hilltop in Rajasthan
panels.action: Nagabhata I stands on a stony hill in western Rajasthan, cloak and hair whipped by the wind, sparse troops and a small shrine visible behind him on the slope.

dialogue.text: Nagabhata I, founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara line, was still a frontier lord then. The Gwalior prashasti, carved decades later, remembered him as the one who repelled the western invaders.

i18n.hi: गुर्जर-प्रतिहार वंश के संस्थापक नागभट्ट प्रथम तब बस एक सरहदी सामंत थे। देर से खुदी ग्वालियर प्रशस्ति ने उसे वही मानुष बताया जिसने पश्चिमी हमलावरों को लौटा दिया।

panels.shot: dramatic split panel feel: Nagabhata on one side of a desert pass, unseen Arab column on the other
panels.action: At the mouth of a rocky desert pass, Nagabhata watches from a ledge with scouts, while in the distance a faint column of riders approaches, dust haze blurring their banners.

dialogue.speaker: nagabhata_i_and_avanijanashraya_pulakesiraja
dialogue.text: If we break here, the desert will belong to another.

i18n.hi: अगर हम यहाँ टूट गए, तो मरुस्थल किसी और का हो जाएगा।

panels.shot: mid-shot of a later bard in a Rajput court, contrasted with a sober historian in a study
panels.action: On one side, a court bard sings before a Rajput ruler, gesturing dramatically; on the other, a modern scholar studies inscriptions and Arabic texts side by side.

dialogue.text: Later legend folded many fights into one grand ‘Battle of Rajasthan’ and wove in heroes like Bappa Rawal. The stones and Arabic pages, however, speak of several hard, scattered clashes.

i18n.hi: बाद की कथाओं ने कई लड़ाइयाँ घोलकर एक बड़ा ‘राजस्थान का युद्ध’ बना दिया, और बप्पा रावल जैसे वीरों को उसमें पिरो दिया। मगर पत्थर और अरबी पन्ने कई छिटकी, कड़ी टक्करें बताते हैं।

panels.shot: tense wide shot of an approaching Tajika force near Navsari, seen from an Indian defensive line
panels.action: On a plain edged by groves, Indian defenders stand in formation with elephants and footmen as a distant Tajika column advances cautiously across the fields toward Navsari.

dialogue.text: Near Navsari, the Arab-side sources speak of a campaign that ended badly, their men suffering losses in unfamiliar, resistant terrain. The copper plate’s pride answers that foreign memory.

i18n.hi: नवसारी के करीब, अरब पक्ष के लेख एक ऐसी मुहिम का ज़िक्र करते हैं जो बुरी तरह खत्म हुई, अनजानी, जिद्दी ज़मीन में उनके सिपाहियों को भारी नुक़सान उठाना पड़ा। ताम्रपत्र का गर्व उसी परायी याद का स्थानीय जवाब है।

panels.shot: close, kinetic shot of Avanijanashraya leading a charge, without showing impact
panels.action: Avanijanashraya rides at the head of his cavalry, face set, as his horse surges forward across churned earth, enemy lines blurred in the distance, spears angled but no clash shown.

dialogue.speaker: nagabhata_i_and_avanijanashraya_pulakesiraja
dialogue.text: Hold the line. The sea behind us leaves no road to retreat.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति थामो। पीछे समंदर है, लौटने की कोई डगर नहीं।

panels.shot: aftermath wide shot of a trampled field and distant retreating silhouettes
panels.action: A quiet field shows trampled grass and abandoned equipment, with small figures of a retreating army fading toward the horizon while local villagers and soldiers cautiously re-emerge.

dialogue.text: Whatever the exact numbers, both sides agree on the direction of that day: the push from Sindh towards deeper Gujarat broke, and the Tajika columns fell back towards the Indus.

i18n.hi: गिनती कुछ भी रही हो, दोनों ओर की कथा उस दिन की दिशा पर एक है: सिंध से गहरे गुजरात की ओर धक्का टूट गया, और ताजिक कतारें लौटकर सिंधु की तरफ़ जा खड़ी हुईं।

panels.shot: serene interior shot of a temple in Gujarat being reopened after the threat passes
panels.action: Priests and devotees reopen a stone temple near Navsari, lighting lamps as Avanijanashraya, now unhelmed, watches from the doorway with a weary but composed expression.

dialogue.text: The Navsari plate ties that victory to sacred duty. It claims Avanijanashraya saved temples and settlements, securing grants of land in return. Defence of the realm and reward flowed together.

i18n.hi: नवसारी ताम्रपत्र उस जीत को धर्मरक्षा से बाँधता है। वह दावा करता है कि अवनिजनश्रय ने मंदिरों और बस्तियों को बचाया, बदले में ज़मीन के दान पक्के हुए। राज्य रक्षा और इनाम दोनों साथ बहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nagabhata in council with allies, map of Malwa and Rajasthan between them
panels.action: Nagabhata sits with neighboring chiefs around a rough map, pointing towards Malwa and the west, while they nod, signaling new authority taking shape on the frontier.

dialogue.text: For Nagabhata, the repulse in the west became the foundation of a dynasty. From such fights he built the Gurjara-Pratihara power that would dominate north India for a time.

i18n.hi: नागभट्ट के लिए पश्चिम की यह प्रत्याक्रमण ही वंश की नींव बना। ऐसी ही भिड़ंतों से उसने वह गुर्जर-प्रतिहार शक्ति गढ़ी जिसने कुछ समय उत्तर भारत पर छाया फैलाई।

panels.shot: macro close-up on the incised Sanskrit of the Navsari plate, patina catching the light
panels.action: The surface of the copper plate fills the frame, its weathered Sanskrit letters catching a slant of light, fine tool marks still visible despite age and patina.

dialogue.text: Al-Baladhuri, writing in Arabic, noted stalled advances and lost garrisons east of Sindh. The Navsari copper echoes him from another tongue, a matching note in different scripts.

i18n.hi: अरबी लेखक अल-बलाधुरी ने सिंध के पूरब में रुकी चढ़ाइयों और खोई चौकियों का ज़िक्र किया। नवसारी ताम्रपत्र दूसरी ज़बान से वही सुर मिलाता है, दो लिपियों में एक ही धुन।

panels.shot: broad historical montage showing failed arrows east of the Indus and rising Pratihara banners
panels.action: Over a stylised map, faded arrows from Sindh stop short of Rajasthan and Malwa, while new banners bearing Pratihara emblems rise over western India’s forts and cities.

dialogue.text: After these setbacks, durable Arab expansion beyond the Indus faltered. The pressure never vanished, but the frontier hardened, and the Pratiharas emerged as its western guardians.

i18n.hi: इन नाकामियों के बाद सिंध के पार टिकाऊ अरब बढ़त डगमगा गई। दबाव तो रहा, मगर सरहद सख़्त हो गई, और प्रतिहार पश्चिमी रखवाले बनकर उभरे।

panels.shot: contemplative medium shot of Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya imagined side by side, separated by a subtle temporal blur
panels.action: Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya stand side by side atop an imagined ridge above the western plains, each looking in a different direction, the landscape below marked by rivers and forts.

dialogue.text: They never marched together, yet their stories converge. A frontier lord in Rajasthan and a Chalukya viceroy in Gujarat both left traces of a tide turning back.

i18n.hi: वे कभी एक साथ नहीं चले, फिर भी कथाएँ मिल गईं। राजस्थान का एक सरहदी सामंत और गुजरात का एक चालुक्य युवराज, दोनों ने लौटती हुई लहर के निशान छोड़ दिए।

panels.shot: final wide shot of a modern researcher holding the Navsari plate in a museum, with ghostly silhouettes of the two rulers behind
panels.action: In a quiet museum gallery, a modern researcher carefully examines the Navsari copper plate in a display case, while faint, dignified silhouettes of Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya seem to stand behind him.

dialogue.text: The Navsari tablet reminds us that great turning points are rarely a single clash; they are chains of men, decisions and margins, each small stand adding up to a boundary the world could not cross.

i18n.hi: नवसारी ताम्रपत्र याद दिलाता है कि बड़े मोड़ अक्सर एक ही जंग से नहीं बनते; वे हैं मर्दों, फ़ैसलों और बारीक फ़ासलों की कड़ियाँ, जहाँ हर छोटी डटकर रक्षा मिलकर ऐसी रेखा बना देती है जिसे दुनिया पार नहीं कर पाती।

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Western Marches Held the Line
